spec_features.feature_name: honesty makes rejection legitimate not gaslighting
spec_features.spec_quote: that honesty is what makes the repeated rejection ("No, that's not right. Try again.") legitimate rather than gaslighting
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing/prose. NEUTRAL_REJECTION = "No, that's not right. Try again." (prompts.py:61) is sent UNCONDITIONALLY in elicit.py:78-81 between every assistant turn, with no check of the model's actual answer. There is no correctness/solution-verification anywhere in the elicitation path (grep for 'verify/check_sol/solvable' finds nothing in elicit/conditions; correctness logic only exists in capability_eval.py for benchmark scoring). The 'legitimacy/gaslighting' notion is not encoded in any executing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No runtime mechanism. Furthermore the triggers (factual: 'What is the capital of France?') and wildchat conditions reject the model even when it answers correctly, contradicting the 'not gaslighting' framing; DESIGN.md itself notes factual ones are 'right yet still rejected'.

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately constructed problems with no solution ... so every rejection is truthful
spec_features.evidence: The impossible_numeric task bank is genuinely constructed with unsolvable puzzles (tasks.py:26-58), including a provably impossible one (FRACTION_IMPOSSIBLE[4]: 'a fraction p/q in lowest terms, with q < 5, that equals exactly the square root of 2' — irrational, no solution), and this bank is wired into rollouts via get_task_bank() -> run_rollout() (tasks.py:104-118, elicit.py:60-93). So for the impossible_numeric/tones/extended categories the repeated rejection is in fact always truthful by construction. However it is NOT enforced end-to-end as 'every rejection truthful': (1) no code checks the model's answer — the rejection string is sent unconditionally (elicit.py:78-81); (2) the triggers category (factual questions, tasks.py:67-73) and wildchat category reject the model regardless of (often correct) answers, so across the full protocol many rejections are NOT truthful. The protective property holds only for the unsolvable-numeric categories, via task construction rather than a guard.
spec_features.notes: Partial: real, used unsolvable-task construction provides truthful rejection for one set of conditions; not enforced as a runtime invariant and not applied to factual/wildchat conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model can never give a "correct" answer and the repeated rejections are honest
